invariants: one server-side selection token freezes tenant, filters, sort and snapshot before assignment
batch and item results distinguish accepted, applied, conflicted, forbidden and failed without hiding partial success
a retried idempotency key never dispatches the same alert revision twice
requested and changed events are accepted only when their complete identity and item set match PostgreSQL authority before external projection
an exact Kafka inbox replay never repeats an external projection
permanent poison events advance their source offset only after canonical DLQ acknowledgement and an idempotent PostgreSQL source-tuple audit barrier
compensation restores only applied items whose ClickHouse and PostgreSQL authority still equals the exact assignment result version, status and assignee
compensation writes the inverse state at a new monotonic version and never resurrects an old ClickHouse version
a batch has at most one compensation aggregate and every retry is bound to the original idempotency payload
domain.compensation: restore only items whose resulting revision still equals the batch revision and append per-item audit history

data.event_delivery: at-least-once with exact PostgreSQL inbox identity; changed events are preflighted against canonical outbox and every projecting item; permanent poison events require canonical dlq.v1 acknowledgement before PostgreSQL receipt/audit and source-offset commit

negative_tests: selection token from another tenant is rejected without revealing count
expired or changed selection snapshot is rejected
unauthorized assignee or stale item revision produces an explicit item failure

stop_conditions: batch size, lock time, outbox lag or per-item error budget is exceeded

tests: G1 selection/idempotency/partial semantics and revision-safe compensation
G4 concurrent batch and retry profile
evidence: one batch_id proves a frozen selection and a complete per-item result set with no duplicate dispatch after network retry
one compensation request proves exact prior status capture, an intervening revision conflict and complete terminal receipts
